Chunk Text:
The Plant shall be designed as a Combined Cycle Power Plant, consisting of but not limited to:
- Dual Fuel Gas Turbine (GTs)
- Dry low NOx combustors;
- Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSGs),
- By-pass  stack  including  diverter  dampers  horizontal  and  vertical  sealing  guillotine damper.
- Condensing Steam Turbine (CST) with Air Cooled Condenser
- Synchronous Generators for Gas Turbines and Steam Turbine
- Generator Circuit Breakers for GTGs and STGs
- 2 winding Generator Step-up transformers;
- 2 or 3 winding Auxiliary transformers
- HV Circuit Breakers for GSU Transformers of GTGs and STG
The plant shall be designed preferably symmetrically; this means the Plant shall consist of equally designed Groups (same number and type of GTs/HRSGs/ST).

Chunk Text:
The steam turbine outlet connection pieces shall be designed for smooth transition with minimal obstructions from the LP turbine exhaust to the condenser to assure negligible pressure drop.
The turbine bypass dumps shall be designed with dispersion headers internal to the condenser to adequately disperse the steam safely into the condenser for all possible extreme transient scenarios.
The Air-Cooled condenser materials shall be selected to provide the necessary reliability at an economical cost taking into account that ACC is being operated with Demineralized water with proper water chemistry required by OEM guidelines. ACC OEM Design will take into consideration of proper material selection as per Demin water quality..
Vacuum raising and maintaining plant may be based on either steam ejectors or mechanical vacuum pumps. As a minimum, one start-up (hogging) duty and one running duty device shall be provided for each condenser.
Steam for air ejectors, if supplied, shall be taken from the main steam supply. A silencer shall be provided on each ejector outlet.
The hotwell tank and condensate system shall be sized in accordance with HEI standards.
The condensate system shall be equipped with instrumentation that will assist in trouble shooting of any condenser tube leakage.

The Fuel Connection Facility for gas will be located so that the area is directly accessible by Saudi Aramco from the outside without using the main gate of the Plant.
The EPC Contractor shall supply all civil works required for gas station according to the requirements for Rumah and Nairyah. This gas station shall be of sufficient size for any receiving/reducing/booster pumping installations along with the required metering necessities, I&C and electrical requirements.
The design for the gas installations shall be carried out in close coordination with SPPC and Saudi Aramco

Chunk Text:
The HRSG shall be designed and sized based on the Design Point Performance (to be chosen at a later stage) operating on natural gas specified on OTS Part A Annex 4.1-1 Fuel Gas Specification.
The  HRSG  shall  be  equipped  with  cold  end  condensate  recirculation  system  and  condensate  bypass arrangement. The HRSG shall achieve the desired plant performance at all the operating points.
In  case  of  cold  casing  design,  the  HRSG  design  shall  incorporate  adequate  hot  &  cold  end  corrosion protections. Hot and Cold end corrosion protective measures shall include Protective coatings on the casing and protective layers (Teflon or other suitable corrosion protection layers) to minimise the undesirable effects of sulphuric acid corrosion. Alternatively, hot casing design for HRSG shall be provided for hot and cold  end  corrosion  protection.  The  corrosion  protection  methods  employed  shall  be  having  proven commercial operational experience and shall be approved by the OWNER.
To satisfy the operational requirement as mentioned in OTS Part A. In order to model the degradation due to aging, the following information shall be supplied for HRSG for years following post COD starting from guaranteed values, but applying best estimate degradation in addition to submitting the long-term best estimate degradation curve or factors:
- Enthalpy of the exhaust gas
- Mass flow of the exhaust gas
- Temperature of the exhaust gas
- Exhaust Gas composition
- The pressure, temperature and steam flow of each pressure level
HP steam, after expansion in the HP ST, can be equally split over 2 or 3 HRSGs for reheating, without creating unbalances in the respective HRSGs (if reheat system is applied).
Condensate return temperature shall be above dew point temperature, to minimize corrosion risk.

The  Contractor  will  be  required  to  design  and  construct  the  Plant  in  accordance  with  the  applicable environmental laws and standards. The Contractor is also responsible for obtaining and maintaining all the necessary Permits for the construction of the Plant.
An Environmental Impact Assessment Study (EIA) will be completed by Owner and copy of the same will be made available to Contractor. A Preliminary Environmental Assessment ('PEA') or Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ('E S IA') was conducted by the Offtaker and is provided in OTS Part A, Annex 3.31 of Part III (Drawings and Diagrams).
It is anticipated that the Project's development will necessitate the involvement of international lenders for financing. Given this, the Project's assessment will need to account for the requirements of international lenders in addition to the local regulations. With the specific international lenders currently unknown, the key requirements, which have been considered within this Scoping report, comprise the Equator Principles III (2013) and associated IFC Performance Standards (2012). The Project will be expected to comply with the most stringent standards should national/IFC requirements differ.
The Owner will progress the EIA Study with the intention that the Environmental Permit is available soon after the time of Contract Award. Contractor shall be responsible for providing all the necessary technical and environmental inputs to the extent required for the EIA study. After Contract Award any amendment to  the  EIA  Study  and  the  Environmental  Permit  will  be  the  responsibility  of  the  Owner  and  the  EPC Contractor.
Waste management during construction will be in accordance with the Waste Management Plan developed specifically for this project and in accordance with Government and Company approved plan.
Hazardous  Area  Classification  drawings  shall  be  developed  in  accordance  with  the  latest  revision  of ANSI/API  RP-505  and  Company  Standard  SAES-B-068  during  the  PP  Phase.  The  Area  Classification drawings shall be prepared from the project plot plans and the process schedule of hazardous materials to determine the potential sources of hazard.
All areas of the where concentrations of gas may occur due to normal leakage or process fault or ventilation system failure shall be classed as hazardous locations. The Contractor shall calculate and produce area classification drawings and documentation for the whole site area. The classified area shall be as defined within the relevant regulations and standards. All equipment within each area shall be uniquely identified and be fully compliant with the standards and regulations.

All plant shall run without undue vibration and with the least practicable amount of noise.

The sewage treatment plant and its ancillary systems shall fulfil the requirements to collect, treat/clarify and discharge the domestic and sanitary waste waters streams. The industrial wastewater shall be treated separately in adequate system. Both, domestic and industrial wastes consist of many compounds which could contaminate surface water) groundwater and soil. Furthermore, especially in the case of discharging untreated sanitary wastewater, the bacteriological contamination can result in the occurrence and spread of water borne diseases like cholera, dysentery, typhoid, etc. Therefore, special attention has to be paid by the Contractor during its investigation of the wastewater collection area to ensure that all waste water streams are considered and will be segregated, collected and discharged in a wastewater collecting system. This also includes all the sanitary and other domestic wastewater out of all permanent and temporary site facilities and the industrial wastewater out of the process like backwash water, rinse water, chemical and acid cleaning wastes and other process wastewater which cannot be used in other ways (blow-down water, etc.).
The wastewater shall be delivered to the wastewater treatment plant in sewers or pipes made of customary and proven materials in adequate diameters according to the amount of wastewater conducted in the pipes. In the case of geodetic constraints, pumping stations must be installed in adequate numbers. In the case of using cesspools, intermediate storage is allowed. The cesspools  must be emptied by vacuum loader(s), which are also part of the scope of supply.
The collected wastewater should be treated in accordance with the above effluent limits.
In order to meet the required quality of clarification, sanitary and domestic wastewater streams should at least be treated by screening and primary sedimentation, biological clarification in activated sludge basins, sedimentation for removing the activated sludge and as a last stage an effluent disinfection for discharging
the wastewater into the sea. The treated sanitary wastewater should also be used for irrigation purposes if required.
All wastewater streams discharged into the domestic waste water treatment plant shall be free of toxic and inhibitory compounds concerning the process of biological clarification or compounds that can influence the further use of the sewage sludge.
The sewage sludge should either be treated or dried for use as fertilizer or disposed of in a suitably designed landfill according to US EPA/EU specification.
In  order  to  meet  the  required  quality  values,  industrial  wastewater  should  be  treated  separately  with special regard to the parameters listed in Table above.
Special regard is to be paid by the Contractor to the contamination of the several streams and the adequacy and suitability of treatment process wastewater streams with similar contamination can be summarized and mixed before treatment. Oil contaminated water have to be treated in oil separators.

The RAM modelling effort  has  several  objectives  based  on  the  activity's  timing  and  the  level  of  detail incorporated in the model.
The main goals of the RAM assessment shall be:
- To test the capacity assumptions used in the initial design documents, at the unit and plant level, and identified equipment, systems or other factors contributing to the generation losses
- To  calculate  the  design  inherent  reliability  of  the  plant  represented  by  electrical  power continuity  of  supply reliability,  based  on  the  final  design  of  the  plant,  including  a  sensitivity analysis  in  order  to  determine  the  effect  on  reliability  output  changes  in  the  different  input parameters
- Definition  of  conditions  or  assumptions  under  which  that  calculated  reliability  can  be maintained as representative of the 'reliability of the plant operation'. Especially the related considerations of aspects, additional to design, that affect to the final achievable reliability like those which would be in the scope in the Operation & Maintenance of the plant stage.

The RAM assessment shall consider all systems, packages, sub-systems and equipment associated with all generating units of the plant and their utilities/ancillary systems/equipment required to maintain their operational status. The assessment will be divided in each unit and facility.
Finally, results of each specific unit and facility will be combined to assess overall reliability of the Plant. In the assessment, all relevant aspects that affect the expected reliability of the Plant shall be considered.
All systems that affect to electrical generation of the plant should be considered in the RAM assessment (to be discussed between the parties).

Chunk Text:
The RAM assessment to be developed by the EPC Contractor and shall include the following:
- The RAM software to be employed to perform calculations shall be based on Monte Carlo methodology and performed using Isograph.
- International standard EN-60812 or similar shall be considered.
- Establish a Base Case Model with all assumptions, including equipment reliability data used in the assessment.
- Prepare  Reliability  Block  Diagrams  (RBDs),  including  but  not  limited  to  configuration, sparing, and sizing arrangements. The RBD shall accurately model the system failure logic and include all redundancy in each specific system.
- Prepare a list of equipment or systems considered in the model with the Failure Mode and Failure Rates included in the models (MTTF, MTTR).
- Prepare a Base Case Model analysis, providing recommendations for the improvement of overall  reliability.  Perform  sensitivity  analyses,  for  the  recommended  parameters  or equipment or for the client chosen parameters after analysing the first base case draft.
- Model uncertainty related to equipment failure, to prevent potential effects on the process and identify appropriate actions that will lead to reduced consequences
- RAM analysis shall be developed 'top-down' and expanded to lower levels.
- Expected average Plant availability and reliability
- Identification of all potential critical components and process bottlenecks
- Identification of failure modes and their consequences
- Decision  support  to  determine  the  most  cost-optimal  solution  to  improve  reliability results with respect to:
- Process design
- Spare part philosophy
- Mobilization times and contracts
- Preventive maintenance strategy
- Identification of cost-effective measures
- Knowledge of industry performance methodology

Chunk Text: An appropriate level of redundancy shall be included in each auxiliary system. The Plant shall be designed so that no single auxiliary equipment failure or trip (except main equipment) shall result in the reduction of power capacity. In this context, it is required that all critical auxiliary equipment shall be provided with N+1  configuration.  Station  (common)  auxiliaries  shall  include  similar  redundancy  such  that  no  single equipment failure shall result in any loss of Plant generating capacity. Main equipment refers to all GTs, HRSGs,  STs,  GRMS,  condensers,  generators,  main  transformers,  aux.  transformers,  major  electrical equipment,  cables,  pre-treatment.  Redundant  backup  equipment  shall  start  instantaneously  to  enable continued functioning of the process without consequent malfunction.

All  pumps  and  compressors  shall  be  redundant  with  on-line  switchover  capability  with  following redundancy:
- Pumps, blowers, compressors, fans : N+1
- Lube oil pump for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Lube oil heater for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Power Plant Jockey pumps : 2x100%
- Heat exchangers (not applicable to fin fan cooler or to air cooled condenser). Redundancy should be considered to eliminate single point of failure that will result in reduced load.
- Cooling tower/fin fan cooler cells : N+1
- Tanks (if not mentioned hereunder) : more than 1
- CCW Expansion Tanks : 1 x 100%
- Atmospheric drain tank : 1 x 100%
- Vacuum Flash Tank : 1 x 100%
- Condensate Storage Tank : 2x50% or 1x100%
- Service air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- Instrument air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- H2 Tanks : 2 x 50%
- Diesel storage tank : 2 x 50%
- Gas Drain Collection Tank (GT Area) : 1 x 100%
- GT Fuel Gas Last Chance Filter (per GT) : 2 x 100% Chemical tanks
- DM plant : N+1 stream
- Air conditioning :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house)
- Ventilation Fans :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house))
- Gas reducing station : 3 x 50%
- Feed water control stations : 2 x 100%
- Fuel Gas Boosting Compressors: : N+1, where, N=Number of Gas Turbines
- Air  compressors  with  after  coolers  (after  coolers  if  required,  will  be  confirmed  during  detail engineering) : 3x50%
- Air filtering skids : 2 x 100%
- Air dryers : 2 x 100%
- After Filters : 2 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each GT : 1 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each ST : 1 x 100%
- N2 rack & manifold station : 1 x 100%
- H2 generator : 2 x 100%
- Drain and vent valves :  two  valves  in  series  (If  operating  pressure  is greater than 4 MPa) otherwise single valve
- Level control valve for HRSG Drums and Feedwater tank :  N+1 (not applicable for startup line, as applicable)
Provision of bypass valves for control valves shall apply for those systems/facilities which can also be reasonably controlled manually.

Chunk Text:
- No single main equipment (GTU, STU, GSUT and HRSG) failure shall result in a Forced Outage of the entire Plant.
- No single auxiliary equipment (all other equipment than main equipment as specified above) failure shall result in the Forced Derating of Plant. The compliance with the above criterion requires to a large extent  redundancy  of  the  entire  auxiliary  equipment.  Following  examples  shall  illustrate  this requirement:
- The Plant shall have a redundant power supply concept for the auxiliary services (redundant UATs, MV - distributions, LV- distributions, DC-system, UPS- system)
- Electronic devices of the protection systems must be redundant in case process redundancy is not available, while the requirement doesn't apply to MV&LV protection relay.
- Redundant active equipment shall be powered from separate buses and physically segregated where feasible. The system design shall be such that the standby equipment shall be activated automatically when the control system detects a failure of the running equipment to perform its intended function.
- GT MCC shall have the redundant / double incoming CB, and divided to two buses, normal bus and essential bus bar, with bus-coupler.

Chunk Text:
- The capacity of MV, LV bus sections and the sources feeding the bus sections should be adequate to take the load of the other bus section when the bus coupler closes in case of supply failure to other bus section.
- The n-1 redundancy criteria shall be maintained for each switchboard/MCC.
- Redundancy shall be provided for cooling fans such that with one group of fan or oil pump out of service the transformer would deliver the rated output within the specified temperature rise.
- Battery and battery chargers shall be provided with N+ 1 redundancy. DC System contains 2 x 100 % Battery and 2 x 100 % Battery Chargers to meet the redundancy requirements.
- UPS shall be provided with N+ 1 redundancy.
- Each LV system switchboard shall consist of two bus sections with two incomers and one bus- coupler. Each incomer shall be supplied by 1x100% capacity transformer.
- Diesel Generator shall be provided with N+1 criteria, where EDG cum BSDG concept to be adopted. The DG sizing shall consider all possible scenarios, including emergency shutdown during black start operation. Emergency cum BSDG DG sets shall have the capability of testing even if respective block is in normal operation OR when the respective block switchgear bus have no voltage. 1 x 100% battery starting system will be applied for BSEDG.
- All electrical system switchboards shall be labelled for Hazard Risk category (HRC) as per results of ARC Flash assessment study using NFPA 70 or relevant IEC standards (as applicable).
- For Gas turbine package, redundancy concept of LV & DC distribution for equipment supplied by OEM would be of OEM's standard design.

Redundancy for control & instrumentation shall be as given below:
- All redundant instrumentation shall have the hot swap capability. Critical Redundant equipment shall be change over automatically in case of failure one equipment / Instrument. (For Gas turbine package, the hot swap capability is not applicable due to safety reason. Especially, it is not allowed to enter GT enclosure during operation, hence any person cannot access the instruments in GT enclosure.)
- Electronic modules in GT control system shall not be removed while the gas turbine is in operation.
- In general, devices shall be preferred that contain intrinsic safety, to avoid expensive supervision/monitoring installations, possibly subject to failure (In Gas turbine package, explosionproof type instruments will be used in the hazardous area.)
- Where redundant equipment is installed, it shall be possible to perform maintenance and repair works on one equipment while the others are in service.
- Hardware part of controls & instrumentation:
- Turbine GT/ST protection system (fail-safe and dual redundant system), For Gas turbine package GT Protection Panel which will consist of Tricon CX triple modular redundant safety PLC system by Schneider Electric Systems as per Supplier's standard design is considered.
- HRSG-protection (fail-safe and triple modular redundant for BMS)
- Triple redundant transmitters for Plant protection signals such as steam drum and main steam parameters.
- Critical measurements, which are supplied with redundant instrumentation shall be connected to different I/O cards.

Chunk Text:
- All protection signals leading to a trip of the Plant or to a load reduction shall use 2 out of 3 voting logic. For Generator Protection System, signal shall be achieved through 1 out of 2 with two multifunction protective relays shall be provided for generator.
- Other controls can be achieved through 2oo2 or 1oo2 voting as per OEM's recommendations.
- Protection for people and environment shall be considered in SIL study according to IEC 61508 and IEC 61511. Allocation of the safety related function (the SIL loop) and its SIL level will be determined according to result of the SIL study.
- All  control  panels,  control  systems  shall  be  provided  with  redundant control supplies. Control and Protection Panels shall be fed from either two redundant DC Source or redundant AC Source (UPS). So, in case of failure one source, the second standby source will take over automatically and will not have any power interruption. (For Gas turbine package, the power supply of GT control system will be fed from essential AC and DC system as per Supplier's standards and power supply for the Gas turbine equipment and CCR will be fed from UPS.)
- Unit protection shall preferably be independently implemented in separate hardware to the control system(s)  to  avoid  common  mode  failure  and  with  appropriate  redundancy  to  ensure  security  of operation.
- For redundancy provisions of equipment, no single fault within the control system shall cause the failure of the duty equipment and at the same time cause the standby equipment to be unavailable.
- Redundancy in the DCS shall include
- Processer redundancy
- Power supply redundancy
- Network redundancy
- Server redundancy
- I/O card segregation
- I/O  card  redundancy  for  critical  signals  (each  of  the  1oo2  or  2oo3  redundant  signals  will  be hardwired to different I/O cards, with each cabinet having redundant power supplies)
- In the case of redundant signals are connected to the different cards, redundant I/O cards are not required.

Performance correction curves and formulae for the correction of measured performance data at conditions different from the Reference Conditions shall be provided by the contractor for both the primary and the backup fuel:
- Gas Turbine Standard correction curves
- Gas Turbine generator capability curve
- Steam Turbine generator capability curve
- CC Start-up curves
- CC Shutdown curve
- Capacity of GT system vs ambient temperature
- Gas Turbine GSUT capacity curve
- Response capability curve (frequency response chart)
- Emissions table
- Steam turbine load changes
- Power output vs gas pressure
- CC Correction curves (to be provided for):
- Evaporative Cooler ON (Only for Base Load),
- Wet Compression On (only after Evaporative Cooler is ON)
- Evaporative Cooler OFF (Base Load and partial loads)
- Duct Firing On (if applicable)
- o The corrections of the net capacity and net heat rate of the total Plant in combined cycle configuration shall be provided for:
- ambient air temperature
- ambient air humidity
- ambient barometric pressure
- Fuel Gas Lower Heating value (LHV)
- Fuel Gas C:H ratio
- Inlet  Air  Condition  Difference  Between  Cooling  Tower/ACC  and  Gas Turbine
- Grid Frequency
- Power Factor
- Cycle Unaccounted Losses
- Natural Gas Pressure at the Terminal Point
- Natural Gas Temperature at the Terminal Point
- Partial load (only for EVC OFF case)
- Degradation with GT fired hours
- condensate return flow and temperature
- b. Outage modes
The important and different outage modes encountered during the operation shall be furnished by the Contractor. Corresponding H&M balance drawings are to be supplied by the Contractor.
The outage durations of GT, HRSG and ST shall be defined.
The  outage  frequency  shall  be  defined  for  HRSG,  ST  and  GT  (in  line  with  the  typical  LTSA assumptions).
